title: SSE connection-reset repropad
content:
Context / goal:
I'm trying to capture a minimal repro and notes for the intermittent "connection reset" seen when clients stream via SSE (text/event-stream). Symptoms: client sees abrupt disconnect mid-stream, server logs show write errors or upstream RST/FIN. Need a repeatable local repro and a checklist of things to toggle (proxy buffering, chunk sizes, keepalives) to narrow root cause.

Observed behaviors (recent incidents):
- Client: curl --no-buffer -i -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.internal/stream/resp -> stream starts, then after some tokens client prints "curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer"
- Node client: fetch stream ends with "write EPIPE" logging at application layer when pushing responses to client socket
- Server-side logs (worker): write to socket failed: Broken pipe (errno 32) at 2026-03-09 14:12:03.345
- Load balancer (ALB) logs show target response terminated with code ELB_CONN_RESET
- tcpdump shows server -> client TCP packet with payload, then client-side RST (unexpected) sometimes, other times server receives RST from an intermediate proxy.

Commands / repro attempts tried locally:
1) Simple curl, no-buffer:
   curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://localhost:8080/stream
   -> reproduction: yes (about 40% runs)

2) curl with HTTP/1.1 forced and verbose:
   curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer https://localhost:8080/stream
   -> shows "Connection reset by peer" and socket closed after last chunk

3) httpie (streaming):
   http --stream --headers GET https://localhost:8080/stream
   -> also hits reset but less frequently than curl (?), inconsistent

4) python aiohttp client (async generator):
   async with session.get(url, headers={ 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }) as resp:
       async for chunk in resp.content.iter_chunked(16):
           await asyncio.sleep(0.05)  # simulate slow consumer
   -> when consumer sleeps, much higher chance of server hitting write error

5) node netcat test:
   (server writes small "data: x\n\n" messages every 10ms)
   echo -e "GET /stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nAccept: text/event-stream\r\n\r\n" | nc localhost 8080
   -> behaviour: if client is not actively reading (nc paused), server write buffers up to some limit then errors out

6) proxied via nginx locally (reverse proxy config default):
   proxy_buffering on; proxy_request_buffering on; proxy_http_version 1.1;
   -> when behind nginx, issue occurs much more frequently. Turning proxy_buffering off reduces frequency drastically.

7) test with chunk size/flush frequency:
   - Write 1KB per event + flush -> fewer resets
   - Write 16B per event with flush -> more resets
   Hypothesis: small writes increase syscall overhead and push kernel socket send buffer patterns that trigger intermediate proxy timeouts or buffer exhaustion.

Snippets used to reproduce server-side (go pseudocode):
   // naive: write string to ResponseWriter, then flush
   w.Header().Set("Content-Type","text/event-stream")
   for i := 0; i < 1000; i++ {
       _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", payload)
       if fl, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok { fl.Flush() }
       if err != nil { log.Printf("write err: %v", err); break }
       time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
   }
   // observed: err sometimes = write: broken pipe

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Proxy buffering + HTTP/2<->HTTP/1.1 conversion: buffers on proxy cause bursts that exceed some timeout/limits, leading to upstream connection tear-down. Evidence: nginx proxy_buffering off helped.
2) Client-side slow consumer causes server socket send buffer to fill -> kernel returns EPIPE on write once peer closed/timeout. Intermediary (ALB/nginx) may send FIN if it decides to cut idle connection.
3) Kernel TCP settings (sndbuf/rcvbuf) + Nagle interaction: many tiny writes cause poor TCP window utilization and proxies may behave badly.
4) Keepalive/timeouts mismatch across ALB / proxy / server causing mid-stream kill.

Debug checklist / experiments to run:
- Reproduce locally with and without proxy (nginx) to isolate where reset occurs.
- Repeat with small consumer delay (simulate slow client) and fast client to compare.
- Toggle nginx: proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on.
- Test ALB/ingress timeouts: increase idle timeout to > 5m for test.
- Run tcpdump for full 3-party flow (client <-> nginx <-> server) and look for RST/FIN timing relative to last payload.
- strace server process to see write(2) return codes and EPIPE timing.
- Add instrumentation in server to log per-write bytes and error string with timestamp.
- Try aggregating events into larger writes (buffer 200ms of events into one write) to see if issue disappears.
- Test with HTTP/2 disabled on upstream to see if conversion layer is culprit.

Useful one-liners:
- tcpdump capture (client IP 10.0.0.5):
  sudo tcpdump -i any host 10.0.0.5 and port 8080 -w sse-reset.pcap

- quick curl with no buffer and show raw headers:
  curl -v --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://localhost:8080/stream

- node quick consumer to emulate slow read:
  const res = await fetch(url, { headers:{ Accept: 'text/event-stream' } });
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while(true){ const {done, value} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 50)); }

Concrete repro (minimal):
1) Start local go server (above code) listening on :8080
2) Start nginx as reverse proxy with default buffering ON
3) Run curl: curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 http://localhost:18080/stream
4) Observe: after a few dozen events, client sees "Recv failure: Connection reset by peer" and server logs write errors

Notes for next actions:
- Lina: can you try disabling proxy_buffering on our staging nginx and run the same load to reproduce? (staging proxy config name: staging-proxy-1)
- Kai: instrument server to log per-write return values and socket errors with timestamps (include goroutine id).
- I will capture tcpdump on a repro run and attach pcap to INF-4321.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are there any quirks in our runtime's write path that explicitly close the socket on backpressure? (e.g., a watchdog)
- Do any upstream middleboxes generate RST when they see lots of tiny chunks?
- Is HTTP/2 multiplexing and conversion to HTTP/1.1 at proxy boundary causing odd pauses?

Raw error snippets captured:
- server: 2026-03-09T14:12:03.345Z WARN write: broken pipe (errno 32)
- client (curl): curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
- node: Error: write EPIPE at Socket._writeGeneric (internal/streams/writable.js:XXXX:XX)
- ALB: "Target response terminated prematurely" (ELB_CONN_RESET)

End of scratchpad. Will update after staging nginx test and pcap attachment.

-- Arjun
